nodes.title: Group 16 Elements (Chalcogens) & Physical Trends
points: Elements: O (8), S (16), Se (34), Te (52), Po (84); general valence configuration ns² np⁴ (n = 2 to 6).
Atomic & ionic radii increase down the group; electronegativity decreases (O has 2nd highest EN = 3.5 in periodic table).
Electron gain enthalpy anomaly: S (−200 kJ/mol) is more negative than O (−141 kJ/mol) due to small size and compact 2p subshell of oxygen causing interelectronic repulsions.
Anomalous behavior of Oxygen: small size, high EN, absence of vacant d-orbitals; forms pπ-pπ multiple bonds (O=O diatomic gas), whereas sulfur exists as puckered S₈ rings.

formulas.label: General valence configuration (Group 16)
formulas.expr: ns² np⁴ (n = 2 to 6)

formulas.label: Order of negative electron gain enthalpy
formulas.expr: S > Se > Te > Po > O (S is most negative; O is least negative)

nodes.title: Allotropes of Sulfur, Ozone & Sulfur Dioxide
points: Sulfur allotropes: Rhombic (α-sulfur, S₈ crown shape, yellow, stable < 369 K) and Monoclinic (β-sulfur, needle-shaped, stable > 369 K). Transition temperature = 369 K.
Ozone (O₃): Pale blue gas, diamagnetic, bent shape (bond angle 116.8°, bond length 127.8 pm, resonance hybrid); powerful oxidizing agent (oxidizes PbS to PbSO₄, I⁻ to I₂).
Quantitative estimation of O₃: Reacted with excess KI buffered with borate buffer (pH 9.2); liberated I₂ titrated against standard Na₂S₂O₃ using starch indicator.
SO₂: Angular gas (sp²); acts as bleaching agent by reduction (temporary bleach in presence of moisture: SO₂ + 2H₂O → H₂SO₄ + 2[H]); decolorizes acidified KMnO₄.

formulas.label: Lead sulfide oxidation by ozone
formulas.expr: PbS + 4O₃ → PbSO₄ + 4O₂

formulas.label: Ozone estimation reaction
formulas.expr: 2I⁻ + H₂O + O₃ → 2OH⁻ + I₂ + O₂

formulas.label: Bleaching action of SO₂ (temporary)
formulas.expr: SO₂ + 2H₂O → H₂SO₄ + 2[H]; Colored matter + [H] → Colorless matter

nodes.title: Sulfuric Acid: Contact Process & Chemical Properties
points: Contact Process key steps: 1) S + O₂ → SO₂; 2) 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅ catalyst, 720 K, 2 bar, exothermic ΔH = −196.6 kJ/mol); 3) SO₃ + H₂SO₄ → H₂S₂O₇ (oleum); oleum + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄ (96-98%).
Strong dibasic acid: Ka₁ is very large (> 10) forming HSO₄⁻; Ka₂ = 1.2 × 10⁻² forming SO₄²⁻.
Strong dehydrating agent: Chars cane sugar (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ → 12C + 11H₂O); dehydrates formic acid to CO and oxalic acid to CO + CO₂.
Oxidizing agent: Conc H₂SO₄ oxidizes Cu to CuSO₄ + SO₂, C to CO₂ + 2SO₂, and S to 3SO₂.

formulas.label: Contact process catalytic oxidation
formulas.expr: 2SO₂ + O₂ ⇌ 2SO₃ (V₂O₅, 720 K, 2 bar, ΔH° = −196.6 kJ/mol)

formulas.label: Dehydration of sucrose (charring action)
formulas.expr: C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁ (conc H₂SO₄) → 12C (sugar charcoal) + 11H₂O

formulas.label: Oxidation of copper by conc H₂SO₄
formulas.expr: Cu + 2H₂SO₄ (conc) → CuSO₄ + SO₂↑ + 2H₂O

nodes.title: Group 17 Elements (Halogens) & Key Trends
points: Elements: F (9), Cl (17), Br (35), I (53), At (85); valence configuration ns² np⁵. All form X⁻ halide ions.
Electron gain enthalpy anomaly: Cl (−349 kJ/mol) > F (−333 kJ/mol) > Br (−325) > I (−295) due to small size of F and interelectronic repulsions in 2p subshell.
Bond dissociation enthalpy anomaly: Cl-Cl (242.6) > Br-Br (192.8) > F-F (158.8) > I-I (151.1 kJ/mol); F-F is unusually weak due to lone pair-lone pair repulsions in tiny F₂.
Oxidizing power: F₂ > Cl₂ > Br₂ > I₂ (E°(F₂/F⁻) = +2.87 V is highest). F₂ oxidizes water to O₂, while Cl₂ and Br₂ form hypohalous acids.

formulas.label: Negative electron gain enthalpy order
formulas.expr: Cl > F > Br > I (Cl has highest negative Δ_egH in periodic table)

formulas.label: Bond dissociation enthalpy order
formulas.expr: Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂ (F₂ is 3rd due to lone-pair repulsion)

formulas.label: Reaction of Fluorine with water
formulas.expr: 2F₂ + 2H₂O → 4HF + O₂↑

nodes.title: Chlorine, Bleaching Action & Reactions with NaOH
points: Preparation: MnO₂ + 4HCl → MnCl₂ + Cl₂ + 2H₂O; Deacon's process: 4HCl + O₂ → 2Cl₂ + 2H₂O (CuCl₂ catalyst, 723 K).
Reaction with ammonia: Excess NH₃ yields N₂ (8NH₃ + 3Cl₂ → 6NH₄Cl + N₂); Excess Cl₂ yields explosive NCl₃ (NH₃ + 3Cl₂ → NCl₃ + 3HCl).
Reaction with NaOH (temperature dependent): Cold dilute NaOH gives hypochlorite (2NaOH + Cl₂ → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O); Hot conc NaOH gives chlorate (6NaOH + 3Cl₂ → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O).
Bleaching action: Permanent bleach due to oxidation via nascent oxygen in presence of moisture (Cl₂ + H₂O → HCl + HOCl; HOCl → HCl + [O]).

formulas.label: Reaction with cold dilute NaOH
formulas.expr: 2NaOH (cold, dil) + Cl₂ → NaCl + NaOCl + H₂O

formulas.label: Reaction with hot concentrated NaOH
formulas.expr: 6NaOH (hot, conc) + 3Cl₂ → 5NaCl + NaClO₃ + 3H₂O

formulas.label: Bleaching action via nascent oxygen (permanent)
formulas.expr: Cl₂ + H₂O → 2HCl + [O]; Colored substance + [O] → Colorless substance

nodes.title: Interhalogen Compounds & Oxoacids of Halogens
points: Interhalogens (XX'ₙ where n = 1, 3, 5, 7): Covalent, diamagnetic; more reactive than pure halogens (except F₂) because X-X' bond is weaker than X-X bond.
VSEPR Geometries: ClF₃ is Bent T-shaped (sp³d, 2 lone pairs); BrF₅ / IF₅ is Square pyramidal (sp³d², 1 lone pair); IF₇ is Pentagonal bipyramidal (sp³d³, 0 lone pairs).
Oxoacids of Chlorine: Hypochlorous (HOCl, +1), Chlorous (HClO₂, +3), Chloric (HClO₃, +5), Perchloric (HClO₄, +7).
Acidic strength order: HOCl < HClO₂ < HClO₃ < HClO₄ (higher oxidation state and greater resonance stabilization of conjugate base ClO₄⁻).

formulas.label: Geometry of ClF₃
formulas.expr: Bent T-shaped (sp³d hybridization, 3 bond pairs + 2 equatorial lone pairs)

formulas.label: Geometry of IF₇
formulas.expr: Pentagonal bipyramidal (sp³d³ hybridization, bond angles 72° and 90°)

formulas.label: Acidic strength of chlorine oxoacids
formulas.expr: HClO < HClO₂ < HClO₃ < HClO₄ (HClO₄ is strongest inorganic acid)

nodes.title: Group 18 Elements (Noble Gases) & Bartlett's Discovery
points: Elements: He (2), Ne (10), Ar (18), Kr (36), Xe (54), Rn (86); stable ns² np⁶ valence shell (He: 1s²).
Physical properties: Monoatomic, colorless, odorless gases; exceptionally high IE, positive electron gain enthalpies, extremely low boiling points (He has lowest bp = 4.2 K).
Neil Bartlett (1962): Noticed PtF₆ oxidizes O₂ to O₂⁺[PtF₆]⁻; since IE of Xe (1170 kJ/mol) is close to O₂ (1175 kJ/mol), synthesized first noble gas compound Xe⁺[PtF₆]⁻ (red solid).
Uses: Helium in cryogenics, MRI magnets, and deep-sea diving (He-O₂ mixture prevents bends); Neon in advertising signs; Argon in electric lamps to provide inert atmosphere.

formulas.label: First noble gas reaction (Neil Bartlett)
formulas.expr: Xe + PtF₆ (298 K) → Xe⁺[PtF₆]⁻ (red crystalline solid)

formulas.label: General configuration (Noble Gases)
formulas.expr: ns² np⁶ (completely filled octet, maximum stability)

nodes.title: Xenon Compounds: Preparation, Structures & Hydrolysis
points: Preparation: Xe + F₂ (2:1 ratio, 673 K, 1 bar) → XeF₂; Xe + F₂ (1:5, 873 K, 7 bar) → XeF₄; Xe + F₂ (1:20, 573 K, 60-70 bar) → XeF₆.
VSEPR Shapes: XeF₂ is Linear (sp³d, 3 equatorial lone pairs); XeF₄ is Square planar (sp³d², 2 axial lone pairs); XeF₆ is Distorted octahedral (sp³d³, 1 lone pair).
Hydrolysis of XeF₄: Disproportionates into Xe, XeO₃, HF, and O₂ (6XeF₄ + 12H₂O → 4Xe + 2XeO₃ + 24HF + 3O₂).
Hydrolysis of XeF₆: Complete hydrolysis gives explosive solid XeO₃ (pyramidal, sp³); Partial hydrolysis gives XeOF₄ (square pyramidal, sp³d²) and XeO₂F₂ (see-saw, sp³d).

formulas.label: Disproportionation hydrolysis of XeF₄
formulas.expr: 6XeF₄ + 12H₂O → 4Xe + 2XeO₃ + 24HF + 3O₂↑

formulas.label: Complete hydrolysis of XeF₆
formulas.expr: XeF₆ + 3H₂O → XeO₃ (pyramidal, explosive) + 6HF

formulas.label: Partial hydrolysis of XeF₆ to XeOF₄
formulas.expr: XeF₆ + H₂O → XeOF₄ (square pyramidal) + 2HF

nodes.title: High-Weightage Board Questions & Named Structures
points: Bleaching comparison: Cl₂ bleaches by permanent oxidation (via nascent oxygen); SO₂ bleaches by temporary reduction (restored on atmospheric oxidation).

Oxoacids of sulfur structures: H₂SO₄ (tetrahedral, dibasic); H₂S₂O₇ (oleum / pyrosulfuric: contains S-O-S bridge); H₂S₂O₈ (Marshall's acid / peroxodisulfuric: contains −O−O− peroxy linkage, oxidation state of S = +6).
Anomalous fluorine: Only −1 oxidation state (no d-orbitals); HF is liquid at room temperature due to strong intermolecular H-bonding, whereas HCl, HBr, HI are gases.
Aqua regia: Mixture of 3 parts concentrated HCl and 1 part concentrated HNO₃; dissolves noble metals like Au and Pt by forming soluble chloro complexes ([AuCl₄]⁻, [PtCl₆]²⁻).

formulas.label: Marshall's acid peroxy linkage structure
formulas.expr: HO-SO₂-O-O-SO₂-OH (H₂S₂O₈, peroxy linkage −O−O−, S oxidation state = +6)

formulas.label: Oleum pyrosulfuric acid structure
formulas.expr: HO-SO₂-O-SO₂-OH (H₂S₂O₇, contains S-O-S anhydride bridge)

formulas.label: Dissolution of gold in aqua regia
formulas.expr: Au + 4H⁺ + NO₃⁻ + 4Cl⁻ → [AuCl₄]⁻ + NO + 2H₂O

nodes.title: MHT-CET High-Speed Shortcuts & Exception Traps
points: TRAP 1: Electron gain enthalpy: Cl > F (Group 17) and S > Se > Te > Po > O (Group 16; Oxygen has least negative Δ_egH in the whole group!).
TRAP 2: Halogen bond energy: Cl₂ > Br₂ > F₂ > I₂ (Fluorine is 3rd, NOT 1st!).
TRAP 3: Boiling point of Group 16 hydrides: H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te < H₂O (H₂O has highest bp due to H-bonds; H₂S has lowest bp).
TRAP 4: Acidic strength of hydrides: H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te (acidity increases down group as H-E bond energy decreases). Group 17: HF < HCl < HBr < HI.
TRAP 5: Number of lone pairs on Xenon: XeF₂ = 3; XeF₄ = 2; XeF₆ = 1; XeO₃ = 1; XeOF₄ = 1; XeO₂F₂ = 1.
TRAP 6: Cl₂ + NaOH: Cold/dil gives NaOCl (+1 oxidation state); Hot/conc gives NaClO₃ (+5 oxidation state).

formulas.label: Hydride boiling point trend (Group 16)
formulas.expr: H₂S (lowest) < H₂Se < H₂Te < H₂O (highest, 373 K due to H-bonding)

formulas.label: Hydride acidic strength trend (Group 17)
formulas.expr: HF < HCl < HBr < HI (HI is strongest acid due to weakest H-I bond)

formulas.label: Reducing power of Group 16 hydrides
formulas.expr: H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te (H₂Te is strongest reducing agent)
